supporting: FY22–25 share movements identify recurring programmes, including the FY22 treasury component and FY24–25 gross proceeds.
adverse: FY24 aggregate gross-case screen implies about VND 753bn and FY25 about VND 768–932bn before benefits at period reference values. Repeated below-reference issuance raises a capital-allocation concern.
magnitude.limitation: Exact event denominators, contemporaneous value and net proceeds unqualified. Period screens show exposure direction and scale only.

supporting: Audited share movements identify employee programmes. The retained history identifies FY2025 authorization and VND 10,000 issue terms.
adverse: The amount of incremental shareholder value received in return for recurring share awards is unclear. Retained period-specific evidence does not establish contemporaneous cohort-level incentive and retention design across material programmes.
alignment.limitation: Do not import the May/June 2026 cohort terms or recalculated KPIs. The older authorization does not establish the full contract.

supporting: Share movements and year-end disclosures separate newly issued shares and the identified treasury component from mechanical share changes. FY25 authorization is identified.
adverse: Authorization and pro-rata changes do not protect existing holders from the discount on employee issuance.
protection.limitation: Historical cohort-specific restrictions, enforcement, rights scope and event reconciliation cannot be established across the full window.

supporting: Documented comparable EPS pairs and parent NPAT improved across FY2022–25. Group FCF/equivalent share improved over the full window. FY2025 ESG and staff expense provide operating context.
adverse: FY2025 FCF/equivalent share dropped materially. Group turnover is 15.4% and does not identify programme participants or the change caused by ESOP.
outcome.limitation: Group outcomes corroborate resilience only. Aggregate profit, training and productivity cannot be credited as incremental ESOP offsets. No transfer of CA-PSV, BQ-EQ, GQ-INC or RG-GOV points.

annual.judgment: N/R. The pattern supports a meaningful recurrent discount risk, while the eligible historic terms and exposure coverage do not demonstrate programme-wide control or sufficiently establish realized material detriment. The absence of quantified benefits is not the decision predicate.

supporting: June 2026 share basis, gross proceeds and completion price are verified. The programme is close to FY2025 in nominal shares and smaller on the stated percentage measures.
adverse: Approximately 85.88% price discount at the completion-close sensitivity. VND 655.650–688.108bn gross-case hurdle across the window. Historical recurrence and discounted period screens matter.
magnitude.limitation: Completion price may embed anticipated dilution. Net fees, value at authorization, historic event-aligned economics and realized use-of-proceeds returns are unqualified.

supporting: Employee award recognizes FY2025 contribution with a three-year lock. Managers have profit and TSR legs, performance-weighted allocation and a ten-year lock.
adverse: Negative TSR produced zero TSR award while the profit leg remained positive. Cash efficiency is not a standalone trigger. The published formula and completed allocation differ by approximately 5,332 shares.
alignment.limitation: No cause assigned to the reconciliation difference. Contractual duration and plausible retention are not observed benefit duration or incremental value.

supporting: Issuer authorization, signed disclosures, cohort limits, senior lock and original-price resale on voluntary departure during lock are substantive design controls. Pro-rata entitlements are treated separately.
adverse: Below-reference issuance transfers value in the scenarios even with the lock. Retirement, qualifying illness/accident and inheritance exceptions matter. The employee cohort lacks the same verified voluntary departure term.
protection.limitation: No verification of actual resale enforcement, realized limitations on transfer or returns on earmarked working capital. The standalone signed 2025 approval is absent.

supporting: Documented comparable EPS pairs and parent NPAT improved across FY2022–25. Group FCF/equivalent share improved over the full window. FY2025 ESG and staff expense provide operating context.
adverse: FY2025 FCF/equivalent share dropped materially. Group turnover is 15.4% and does not identify programme participants or the change caused by ESOP.
outcome.limitation: Group outcomes corroborate resilience only. Aggregate profit, training and productivity cannot be credited as incremental ESOP offsets. No transfer of CA-PSV, BQ-EQ, GQ-INC or RG-GOV points. FTEL equity accounting changes the scope from January 2026. Prior consolidated outcomes cannot establish a post-FTEL like-for-like programme outcome.

current.judgment: N/R. The terms and filings establish actual design controls, and the documented award size bounds ownership dilution for June. Neither controls the economic transfer across recurring awards. Deep discount, a sizable transfer range, no demonstrated cash-oriented trade-off and weak FY2025 cash corroboration defeat the positive hypothesis. The completion quote and historic screens do not establish net shareholder detriment. Plausible benefits remain uncredited and unknown.
